title: CLAT — Combined: Logical Reasoning + English Language + Current Affairs GK
description: Combined test: Logical Reasoning + English Language + Current Affairs GK for CLAT. 60Q.
subject: clat-reasoning
instructions: Subject: Logical Reasoning + English Language + Current Affairs GK

questions.question: Which of the following can be most logically concluded from the statement about the relationship between processed food consumption and heart disease?

options.text: All individuals who consume processed foods will eventually develop heart disease.
options.explanation: This option is too absolute, as the statement does not claim that all individuals will develop heart disease.

options.text: Limiting processed food intake is the only effective way to prevent heart disease.
options.explanation: This option is too strong, as the statement does not claim that limiting processed food intake is the only way to prevent heart disease.

options.text: There is a strong correlation between regular processed food consumption and the likelihood of heart disease.
options.explanation: This option is supported by the statement, which links regular consumption of processed foods to an increased risk of heart disease.

options.text: Health authorities primarily focus their advisories on diet-related health issues.
options.explanation: This option goes beyond the scope of the given statement, which only discusses the relationship between processed food consumption and heart disease.

questions.explanation: The statement explicitly links regular consumption of processed foods to an increased risk of heart disease, implying a strong correlation.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following can be logically concluded from the statement about literacy rates in India?

options.text: Urban educational initiatives specifically target the gender gap in literacy.
options.explanation: This option is an assumption, as the statement does not provide information about the specific focus of urban educational initiatives.

options.text: The disparities in literacy rates between genders are more pronounced in rural India.
options.explanation: This option is supported by the statement, which states that the gender gap in literacy remains significant, especially in rural areas.

options.text: The overall literacy rate in rural areas has declined despite educational initiatives.
options.explanation: This option contradicts the statement, which says that the overall literacy rate has improved.

options.text: All educational initiatives have failed to address the gender gap effectively.
options.explanation: This option is too absolute, as the statement does not claim that all initiatives have failed.

questions.explanation: The statement directly says that the gender gap in literacy remains significant, especially in rural areas, which means the difference between male and female literacy is greater in rural areas.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following can be logically concluded from the statement about the relationship between loud noise exposure and hearing loss?

options.text: All factory workers will inevitably suffer from hearing loss.
options.explanation: This option is too absolute, as the statement does not claim that all factory workers will develop hearing loss.

options.text: Loud noise is the only potential cause of hearing loss.
options.explanation: This option is too strong, as the statement does not claim that loud noise is the only cause of hearing loss.

options.text: Factory workers, as a group, face an elevated risk of developing hearing loss.
options.explanation: This option is supported by the statement, which notes that many factory workers are exposed to loud noise for extended periods, thereby increasing their risk of hearing loss.

options.text: Factory workers should seek alternative employment to avoid hearing loss.
options.explanation: This option is not a logical conclusion based on the statement, which only discusses the relationship between loud noise exposure and hearing loss.

questions.explanation: The statement directly links prolonged exposure to loud noise to the potential for hearing loss, and notes that many factory workers are exposed to loud noise for extended periods.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following can be most logically concluded from the statement above?

options.text: Logistics companies were unprepared for the surge in online shopping.
options.explanation: The statement does not mention whether logistics companies were prepared or not.

options.text: The number of online shoppers has decreased.
options.explanation: The statement mentions a surge in online shopping, indicating an increase, not a decrease.

options.text: Delivery services are becoming more expensive for consumers.
options.explanation: The statement does not mention anything about the cost of delivery services for consumers.

options.text: There is a growing need for resources in the logistics sector.
options.explanation: The statement explicitly mentions the immense pressure on logistics companies to expand their fleet and hire more personnel, indicating a growing need for resources.

questions.explanation: The statement explicitly mentions the immense pressure on logistics companies to expand their fleet and hire more personnel, indicating a growing need for resources in the logistics sector.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions can be most logically drawn from the passage?

options.text: The government’s policy will fail due to public resistance.
options.explanation: There is no information in the passage to support this conclusion.

options.text: Low-income households will benefit equally from the policy as high-income households.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about the equal benefit of the policy for low-income and high-income households.

options.text: The policy aims to significantly reduce carbon emissions through specific measures.
options.explanation: The passage clearly states the government's goal and the measures to achieve it.

options.text: The critics are correct in asserting that the policy is unrealistic.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide enough information to support the critics' claim.

questions.explanation: The passage states the government's goal (50% reduction in carbon emissions) and the measures to achieve it (solar panels and EV subsidies). The critics' argument does not invalidate the policy's intent, making C the only directly supported conclusion.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following is an assumption underlying the study’s findings?

options.text: Remote workers have more flexible schedules than office workers.
options.explanation: The passage does not mention flexible schedules as a factor in the study.

options.text: The productivity metrics used in the study accurately measure work output.
options.explanation: For the study's comparison to be valid, the productivity metrics must accurately measure work output.

options.text: Stress levels are solely determined by work environment.
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that stress levels are solely determined by work environment.

options.text: Office workers are less productive due to distractions.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about the reasons for office workers' productivity.

questions.explanation: The study compares productivity between remote and office workers. For this comparison to hold, the productivity metrics must be valid.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: The conclusion drawn above is flawed because:

options.text: It assumes all marine creatures are mammals.
options.explanation: The argument does not assume all marine creatures are mammals.

options.text: It commits the logical fallacy of the undistributed middle.
options.explanation: The argument links 'mammals' to 'marine creatures' through 'warm-blooded' without directly connecting the two categories.

options.text: It incorrectly generalizes from a small sample size.
options.explanation: The passage does not mention a small sample size.
The passage does not suggest a misinterpretation of the term 'warm-blooded'.

questions.explanation: The argument incorrectly links 'mammals' to 'marine creatures' through 'warm-blooded,' without directly connecting the two categories.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the CEO’s claim?

options.text: The company’s competitors also saw a 10% profit increase this quarter.
options.explanation: This information does not directly challenge the CEO's claim.

options.text: A major economic downturn occurred in the previous quarter, artificially inflating this quarter’s baseline.
options.explanation: This information suggests the company's growth might be due to a recovery rather than the campaign.

options.text: The marketing campaign was identical to one used five years ago.
options.explanation: The fact that the campaign was used before does not necessarily weaken the CEO's claim.

options.text: Employee productivity remained unchanged during the quarter.
options.explanation: This information does not directly challenge the CEO's claim about the campaign's effectiveness.

questions.explanation: If a major economic downturn occurred, the company’s growth might be due to a recovery rather than the campaign.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the conclusion to hold?

options.text: All students who study regularly are motivated.
options.explanation: Motivation is not necessary for the conclusion to hold.

options.text: All students who passed the exam studied regularly.
options.explanation: This assumption is necessary for the conclusion that all students who study regularly received honors.

options.text: Honors are awarded only to top-performing students.
options.explanation: The conclusion does not require this assumption about how honors are awarded.

options.text: The exam is equally difficult for all students.
options.explanation: The difficulty of the exam is not relevant to the conclusion.

questions.explanation: The conclusion assumes that studying regularly is the only way to pass the exam (and thus receive honors).
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid inference from the passage?

options.explanation: The passage does not provide exact numbers of supporters.

options.text: The true level of support among urban residents is likely between 62% and 68%.
options.explanation: The margin of error (±3%) supports this inference.

options.text: Younger residents are the majority in the city.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about the age distribution of the city's population.

options.text: The survey proves that the ban will be implemented.
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that the survey's results will directly lead to the implementation of the ban.

questions.explanation: The margin of error (±3%) means the true support level is between 62% and 68%.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: The reasoning in the passage is analogous to which of the following?

options.text: If X is true, then Y must follow. Y is true, so X is true.
options.explanation: This option describes a different logical form.

options.text: If X is true, then Y must follow. Y is not true, so X is not true.
options.explanation: This option describes modus tollens, the same logical form as the passage.

options.text: X follows from Y. Y is not true, so X is not true.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the passage's logical structure.

options.text: X is true only if Y is true. Y is true, so X is true.
options.explanation: This option describes a different logical form than the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage follows the structure: 'If P, then Q. Not Q, therefore not P,' which is modus tollens.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the report’s conclusion?

options.text: Cities without bike-sharing programs also saw a reduction in cyclist accidents.
options.explanation: This information does not directly support the report's conclusion about bike-sharing programs.

options.text: In cities with bike-sharing programs, cyclists are more likely to wear helmets.
options.explanation: This information strengthens the causal link between bike-sharing programs and reduced accidents.

options.text: The number of cyclists increased in cities with bike-sharing programs.
options.explanation: An increase in the number of cyclists does not necessarily explain the reduction in accidents.

options.text: Traffic laws in cities with bike-sharing programs are stricter.
options.explanation: Stricter traffic laws are not directly related to the report's conclusion about bike-sharing programs.

questions.explanation: If cyclists in bike-sharing cities wear helmets more often, this could explain the reduction in accidents, strengthening the causal link.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following arguments follows the same logical structure as the passage?

options.text: All birds can fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins can fly.
options.explanation: This option does not follow the same logical structure as the passage.

options.text: All mammals have lungs. Whales are mammals. Therefore, whales have lungs.
options.explanation: This option follows the same logical structure as the passage.

options.text: All books are made of paper. Newspapers are books. Therefore, newspapers are made of paper.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately follow the passage's logical structure.

options.text: All students study. Some students are diligent. Therefore, some diligent students study.
options.explanation: This option does not follow the same logical structure as the passage.

questions.explanation: The original argument uses a universal statement ('All X are Y') to conclude a specific instance ('Z is X, therefore Z is Y').
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the CEO’s claim?

options.text: The company’s market share remained unchanged.
options.explanation: This information does not directly challenge the CEO's claim.

options.text: A new tax law reduced the company’s tax liability by 10%.
options.explanation: This information suggests an alternative explanation for the company's improved profitability.

options.text: Competitors also saw a 20% revenue increase.
options.explanation: The performance of competitors does not directly relate to the CEO's claim about the company's revenue growth.

options.text: The company laid off 10% of its workforce.
options.explanation: Layoffs do not necessarily explain the company's improved profitability.

questions.explanation: The CEO attributes profitability solely to revenue growth, but a reduction in tax liability could also explain improved profitability.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statement about the government's new policy on electric vehicles?

options.explanation: Conclusion II also follows, so this option is incomplete.
Conclusion I also follows, so this option is incomplete.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
options.explanation: Both conclusions are supported by the given statement.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
options.explanation: Both conclusions are logically valid based on the statement.

questions.explanation: Conclusion I follows because reduced import duties typically lower the cost of imported goods. Conclusion II follows because cheaper imports can threaten domestic producers.
questions.hint: Consider the direct and indirect effects of reducing import duties on the market.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: What can be inferred about Rahul's study habits based on his exam performance?

options.explanation: The conclusion is not definitively true but is probable.
The conclusion is supported by the given information.
The conclusion is likely correct based on the given statement.
The conclusion can be inferred from the given information.

questions.explanation: Since consistent study is a necessary condition for good performance, Rahul’s poor result suggests he likely did not study consistently.
questions.hint: Use the contrapositive of the given statement to draw a conclusion.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given implications P → Q, Q → R, R → S?

options.explanation: P → S is a valid transitive conclusion.
S → P is not supported by the given implications.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
options.explanation: Only Conclusion I is valid.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
options.explanation: Conclusion I is valid.

questions.explanation: From P → Q and Q → R, we get P → R; combining with R → S yields P → S. However, S → P is not supported by the given implications.
questions.hint: Use the transitive property of implications to derive the correct conclusion.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which conclusion(s) about the students playing football and cricket is/are correct?

options.explanation: Conclusion I is incorrect as 15 students play neither sport.
Conclusion II is correct as 15 students play only cricket.
Only Conclusion II is correct.
Conclusion II is correct.

questions.explanation: Total playing at least one sport = 30 + 25 – 10 = 45. Students playing neither = 60 – 45 = 15 → Conclusion I is false. Only cricket players = 25 – 10 = 15 → Conclusion II is true.
questions.hint: Use the principle of inclusion-exclusion to calculate the number of students playing each sport.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: What can be concluded about the match being postponed based on the given statement?

options.explanation: The conclusion is invalid because the absence of rain does not guarantee the match will not be postponed.
The conclusion is invalid as it assumes no other reasons for postponement exist.

options.text: The conclusion is probable but not certain
options.explanation: The conclusion is not even probable; it is invalid.
The conclusion can be determined to be invalid based on the given statement.

questions.explanation: The rule is 'If P then Q.' The absence of P (no rain) does not allow us to conclude ¬Q (match not postponed) because other reasons could still postpone the match.
questions.hint: Consider the logical fallacy of denying the antecedent.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: Which conclusion(s) about the factory's production and defect rate is/are correct?

options.explanation: Conclusion I is correct as the defective units decreased from 96 to 36.
Conclusion II is incorrect as the total output did not increase.
Only Conclusion I is correct.
Conclusion I is correct.

questions.explanation: Defective units before = 1200 × 0.08 = 96. Defective units after = 1200 × 0.03 = 36 → Conclusion I is correct. Output remains 1200; the defect rate change does not imply higher production → Conclusion II is false.
questions.hint: Calculate the number of defective units before and after the new system to verify the conclusions.
questions.subject: clat-reasoning

questions.question: What is the most likely meaning of the word 'abysmal' in the context of the company's financial performance?

options.explanation: Correct, as 'abysmal' means extremely poor or bad.
Incorrect, as 'stellar' means excellent.
Incorrect, as 'mediocre' means average or unremarkable.
Incorrect, as 'fluctuating' means unstable or varying.

questions.explanation: 'Abysmal' means extremely bad or appalling, which would contrast with a positive financial performance. However, the sentence implies a negative financial performance, making 'abysmal' a plausible choice.
questions.hint: Consider the contrast implied by 'despite' in the sentence.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The judge’s ruling, though strict, was not _______; it allowed room for reconsideration.

options.explanation: Arbitrary means based on random choice, which does not fit the context of allowing reconsideration.
Lenient means merciful or tolerant, which aligns with allowing room for reconsideration.
Vindictive means spiteful or vengeful, which contradicts the idea of allowing reconsideration.
Capricious means unpredictable, which does not fit the context of a judge's ruling.

questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts the judge's strict ruling with a quality that allows reconsideration. 'Lenient' (merciful) fits best, while 'arbitrary' (random), 'vindictive' (spiteful), and 'capricious' (unpredictable) do not convey the intended meaning.
questions.hint: The ruling was not overly harsh or unfair.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Despite the company’s financial struggles, the CEO insisted on maintaining _______ spending on R&D to innovate.

options.explanation: Exorbitant means excessively high, which contradicts the idea of wise spending.
Prudent means sensible or cautious, which fits the context of maintaining spending despite financial struggles.
Lavish means extravagant, which does not align with the need for wise spending.
Excessive means too much, which contradicts the idea of maintaining spending wisely.

questions.explanation: The CEO’s decision to continue spending despite losses suggests a wise or cautious approach. 'Prudent' (sensible) fits perfectly, while 'exorbitant,' 'lavish,' and 'excessive' imply wastefulness, which contradicts the context.
questions.hint: The spending was done wisely despite financial difficulties.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The lawyer’s argument was so _______ that the jury found it difficult to follow.

options.explanation: Lucid means clear, which contradicts the idea of the jury finding it difficult to follow.
Convoluted means overly complicated, which fits the context of the jury struggling to follow the argument.
Succinct means brief, which does not align with the jury finding it difficult to follow.
Cogent means persuasive, which does not fit the context of the argument being difficult to follow.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'found it difficult to follow' indicates the argument was overly complex. 'Convoluted' (complicated) is the only option that matches this meaning. 'Lucid' (clear), 'succinct' (brief), and 'cogent' (persuasive) are incorrect.
questions.hint: The argument was overly complicated.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The witness’s testimony was _______ by inconsistencies, casting doubt on her credibility.

options.explanation: Bolstered means strengthened, which contradicts the idea of casting doubt.
Undermined means weakened, which fits the context of inconsistencies casting doubt on credibility.
Corroborated means confirmed, which does not align with casting doubt.
Validated means confirmed as accurate, which contradicts the idea of casting doubt.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'casting doubt on her credibility' suggests the inconsistencies weakened her testimony. 'Undermined' (weakened) is the correct choice. The other options imply strengthening or confirming the testimony, which contradicts the context.
questions.hint: The inconsistencies weakened the testimony.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The new policy, which aims to reduce carbon emissions, is widely seen as _______ if not implemented effectively.

options.explanation: Redundant means unnecessary, which does not fit the context of the policy's potential failure.
Futile means pointless or ineffective, which fits the scenario of the policy failing if not implemented effectively.
Laudable means praiseworthy, which does not align with the idea of potential failure.
Obsolete means outdated, which does not fit the context of the policy's potential ineffectiveness.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'if not implemented effectively' implies the policy might fail despite good intentions. 'Futile' (pointless) fits this scenario. 'Redundant' (unnecessary), 'laudable' (praiseworthy), and 'obsolete' (outdated) do not align with the conditional clause.
questions.hint: The policy might be ineffective if not carried out properly.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The diplomat’s speech, though well-intentioned, was criticized for being _______ in addressing the core issue.

options.explanation: Tangential means irrelevant to the main point, which fits the criticism of the speech.
Pertinent means relevant, which contradicts the idea of the speech being criticized for avoiding the core issue.
Exhaustive means thorough, which does not fit the context of the speech being criticized.
Diplomatic means tactful, which does not align with the criticism of the speech.

questions.explanation: The criticism suggests the speech avoided the main topic. 'Tangential' (irrelevant to the main point) is the correct choice. 'Pertinent' (relevant), 'exhaustive' (thorough), and 'diplomatic' (tactful) are incorrect in this context.
questions.hint: The speech did not focus on the main issue.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The company’s decision to relocate was met with _______ from employees, who feared job losses.

options.explanation: Elation means joy, which contradicts the idea of employees fearing job losses.
Trepidation means fear or anxiety, which fits the context of employees fearing job losses.
Indignation means anger, which does not fit the context of fearing job losses.
Apathy means lack of interest, which does not align with the employees' reaction.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'feared job losses' indicates employees were anxious. 'Trepidation' (fear) is the correct choice. 'Elation' (joy), 'indignation' (anger), and 'apathy' (lack of interest) do not fit the context.
questions.hint: The employees felt fear or anxiety about the decision.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The judge’s ruling was based on a _______ interpretation of the law, leaving no room for ambiguity.

options.explanation: Literal means exact or word-for-word, which fits the context of leaving no room for ambiguity.
Liberal means lenient, which does not fit the context of an unambiguous interpretation.
Strict means rigid, but it does not necessarily imply an unambiguous interpretation.
Ambiguous means unclear, which contradicts the idea of leaving no room for ambiguity.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'leaving no room for ambiguity' suggests the interpretation was exact or word-for-word. 'Literal' fits this meaning. 'Liberal' (lenient), 'strict' (rigid but not necessarily unambiguous), and 'ambiguous' (unclear) are incorrect.
questions.hint: The interpretation was exact and precise.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The scholar’s research was praised for its _______ approach, combining historical data with modern theories.

options.explanation: Myopic means short-sighted, which does not fit the context of combining historical and modern theories.
Interdisciplinary means involving multiple disciplines, which fits the context of combining historical data with modern theories.
Dogmatic means rigid in beliefs, which does not align with the research approach.
Superficial means shallow, which contradicts the idea of a praised research approach.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'combining historical data with modern theories' indicates a blend of fields. 'Interdisciplinary' (involving multiple disciplines) is the correct choice. 'Myopic' (short-sighted), 'dogmatic' (rigid), and 'superficial' (shallow) do not fit.
questions.hint: The research involved multiple academic disciplines.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: The CEO’s decision to downsize was met with _______ from shareholders, who saw it as a sign of mismanagement.

options.explanation: Acclaim means praise, which contradicts the idea of shareholders seeing the decision as mismanagement.
Disapproval means negative judgment, which fits the context of shareholders being unhappy with the decision.
Ambivalence means mixed feelings, which does not align with the shareholders' reaction.
Indifference means lack of concern, which contradicts the shareholders' reaction.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'saw it as a sign of mismanagement' implies shareholders were unhappy. 'Disapproval' (negative judgment) is the correct choice. 'Acclaim' (praise), 'ambivalence' (mixed feelings), and 'indifference' (lack of concern) are incorrect.
questions.hint: The shareholders were unhappy with the decision.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The government’s decision to ______ the controversial policy has been welcomed by the public, as it aligns with the citizens’ long-standing demand for reform.

options.explanation: 'Retain' means to keep, which contradicts the public's demand for reform.
'Revoke' means to officially cancel, aligning with the public's demand for reform.
'Reinforce' means to strengthen, which does not fit the context of cancellation.
'Revert' means to return to a previous state, which is not the intended meaning here.

questions.explanation: The sentence implies that the policy was undone or cancelled. 'Revoke' (to officially cancel) fits best. 'Retain' (keep), 'reinforce' (strengthen), and 'revert' (return to a previous state) do not convey the intended meaning.
questions.hint: The public welcomed the decision, suggesting the policy was no longer in effect.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? Despite the initial setbacks in the project, the team managed to ______ the situation by implementing innovative solutions and working through the night.

options.explanation: 'Exacerbate' means to worsen, which contradicts the team's efforts.
'Alleviate' means to reduce, which does not fully capture the team's actions.
'Salvage' means to save from loss or ruin, fitting the context of the team's efforts.
'Stagnate' means to remain unchanged, which does not describe the team's actions.

questions.explanation: The context suggests the team improved or rescued the situation. 'Salvage' (to save from loss or ruin) is correct. The other options mean worsening ('exacerbate'), reducing ('alleviate'), or remaining unchanged ('stagnate').
questions.hint: The team worked hard to improve the project's outcome.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The lawyer argued that the evidence presented by the prosecution was ______, as it failed to establish a clear connection between the accused and the crime.

options.explanation: 'Circumstantial' refers to indirect evidence, but the sentence emphasizes weakness, not indirectness.
'Conclusive' means definitive, which contradicts the lack of clear connection.
'Tenuous' means weak or flimsy, fitting the context of the evidence's lack of strength.
'Irrefutable' means undeniable, which contradicts the lawyer's argument.

questions.explanation: The evidence lacked strength or validity. 'Tenuous' (weak or flimsy) is the best fit. 'Circumstantial' (indirect evidence), 'conclusive' (definitive), and 'irrefutable' (undeniable) are incorrect as they do not match the negative tone of the sentence.
questions.hint: The evidence was weak and did not clearly link the accused to the crime.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The CEO’s decision to ______ the merger was met with skepticism by the board members, who believed it would hinder long-term growth.

options.explanation: 'Expedite' means to speed up, which would not be met with skepticism.
'Abort' means to terminate prematurely, fitting the context of the board's skepticism.
'Accelerate' means to increase speed, which would not be met with skepticism.
'Facilitate' means to make easier, which does not fit the context of stopping the merger.

questions.explanation: The board members disapproved of the merger being stopped. 'Abort' (to terminate prematurely) fits the context. 'Expedite' (speed up), 'accelerate' (increase speed), and 'facilitate' (make easier) imply positive actions, which contradict the skepticism.
questions.hint: The board members were skeptical because they believed stopping the merger would harm growth.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The researcher’s findings were so ______ that even the most skeptical critics had to acknowledge their significance in the field of quantum physics.

options.explanation: 'Dubious' means doubtful, which contradicts the critics' acknowledgment of significance.
'Groundbreaking' means innovative or revolutionary, fitting the context of the critics' acknowledgment.
'Redundant' means repetitive, which does not describe the findings' significance.
'Mundane' means ordinary, which contradicts the critics' acknowledgment of significance.

questions.explanation: The critics acknowledged the findings' importance, so they must have been innovative or revolutionary. 'Groundbreaking' (innovative) is correct. The other options mean doubtful ('dubious'), repetitive ('redundant'), or ordinary ('mundane').
questions.hint: The critics had to acknowledge the findings' significance, implying they were highly innovative.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The judge ruled that the defendant’s testimony lacked credibility because it was ______ with inconsistencies and contradictions.

options.explanation: 'Replete' means filled with, fitting the context of the testimony being full of inconsistencies.
'Fraught' implies stress or tension, which is not the primary issue here.
'Devoid' means lacking, which contradicts the presence of inconsistencies.
'Complemented' means supplemented, which does not describe the testimony's flaws.

questions.explanation: The testimony was full of inconsistencies. 'Replete' (filled with) is the correct choice. 'Fraught' (filled with, but often implies stress), 'devoid' (lacking), and 'complemented' (supplemented) do not accurately describe the situation.
questions.hint: The testimony was filled with inconsistencies, making it unreliable.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The company’s decision to expand into international markets was met with ______ from investors, who were wary of the economic instability in those regions.

options.explanation: 'Enthusiasm' means excitement, which contradicts the investors' wariness.
'Trepidation' means fear or anxiety, fitting the context of the investors' reaction.
'Ambivalence' means indifference, which does not fully capture the investors' fear.
'Apathy' means lack of interest, which does not describe the investors' cautious reaction.

questions.explanation: Investors were cautious due to economic instability, so their reaction was one of fear or hesitation. 'Trepidation' (fear or anxiety) is the correct choice. The other options mean excitement ('enthusiasm'), indifference ('ambivalence' and 'apathy').
questions.hint: Investors were wary, suggesting they felt fear or hesitation about the expansion.
questions.subject: clat-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The professor’s lecture was so ______ that even students with no prior knowledge of the subject found it accessible and engaging.

options.explanation: 'Esoteric' means obscure or understood by only a few, which contradicts the lecture's accessibility.
'Abstruse' means overly complex, which does not fit the context of the lecture being accessible.
'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, fitting the context of the lecture's accessibility.
'Convoluted' means overly complex, which contradicts the lecture's clarity.

questions.explanation: The lecture was clear and understandable despite students' lack of prior knowledge. 'Lucid' (clear and easy to understand) is correct. The other options mean obscure ('esoteric,' 'abstruse') or overly complex ('convoluted').
questions.hint: The lecture was clear and easy to understand, even for beginners.

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The committee’s report was criticized for being overly ______, as it avoided addressing the root causes of the issue and instead focused on superficial observations.

options.explanation: 'Comprehensive' means thorough, which contradicts the criticism of lacking depth.
'Superficial' means concerned with only the obvious, fitting the context of the report's criticism.
'Meticulous' means detailed, which does not describe the report's lack of depth.
'Exhaustive' means thorough, which contradicts the criticism of lacking depth.

questions.explanation: The report was criticized for lacking depth and addressing only surface-level issues. 'Superficial' (concerned with only the obvious) is the correct choice. The other options mean thorough ('comprehensive,' 'exhaustive') or detailed ('meticulous').
questions.hint: The report was criticized for focusing only on surface-level issues, not the root causes.

questions.question: Which international human rights instrument, adopted in 1948, explicitly recognizes the right to freedom from torture and other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment?

options.text: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), 1966
options.explanation: The ICCPR, adopted in 1966, also prohibits torture under Article 7, but it was not the first instrument to do so.
The UDHR, adopted in 1948, explicitly recognizes the right to freedom from torture in Article 5.

options.text: Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), 1989
options.explanation: The CRC, adopted in 1989, prohibits torture but was not the first instrument to do so.

options.text: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD), 1965
options.explanation: The ICERD, adopted in 1965, addresses racial discrimination but not specifically torture.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B) Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), 1948. Article 5 of the UDHR states, 'No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.' While other instruments also prohibit torture, the UDHR was the first to explicitly recognize this right in 1948.

The UDHR was adopted by the UNGA on 10 December 1948 and is the foundational document for modern human rights law.

options.text: Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), 1989
options.explanation: The CRC was adopted in 1989, much later than 1948.
The ECHR was adopted in 1950, not 1948.

questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UNGA on 10 December 1948 and is the first global expression of rights to which all human beings are inherently entitled.

questions.question: In the landmark judgment *K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India* (2017), the Supreme Court of India recognized which of the following as a fundamental right?

The Supreme Court recognized the right to privacy as a fundamental right in *K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India* (2017).

options.text: Right to free speech in print media
options.explanation: The right to free speech is already recognized under Article 19(1)(a), but the judgment specifically addressed the right to privacy.

questions.explanation: The nine-judge bench unanimously held that the right to privacy is protected as a fundamental right under Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the *Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989*:
I. It was amended in 2018 to include new categories of offences.
II. The Act provides for a mandatory minimum punishment of six months imprisonment.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.explanation: Statement I is correct as the 2018 amendment included new categories of offences. Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II is incorrect because the Act does not provide for a mandatory minimum punishment of six months for all offences.
Only Statement I is correct; Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is correct, so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: The 2018 amendment expanded the definition of atrocities and added new crimes such as garlanding with footwear and disrobing. Statement II is incorrect because the Act prescribes minimum punishment of six months *only for certain offences*, not all.
